name: Ronni Zehavi
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, HiBob (HR software, London/Tel Aviv/New York)
profile: Israeli serial entrepreneur who co-founded HiBob in Tel Aviv in 2015, maker of the 'Bob' cloud HR/HCM platform for mid-sized, distributed companies. HiBob has raised several $150M rounds (valued ~$2.7B in 2023) and has added payroll (Pento, 2024) and FP&A (Mosaic, 2025) via acquisitions. He remains CEO.
interesting_fact: Before HiBob he co-founded content-delivery startup Cotendo in January 2008 (backed by Sequoia and Benchmark), which Akamai bought in March 2012 for over $300M - he calls HiBob his third company.
deep_cut_fact: Cotendo was founded by three former Commtouch (later Cyren) colleagues - Zehavi, Udi Trugman and David Drai - with R&D in Netanya, Israel and HQ in Sunnyvale; it set out to challenge Akamai and ended up being acquired by it.
notes: No published press email found on hibob.com; press page and general Contact Us form are the official routes. Frequent podcast guest on HR/future-of-work topics (Josh Bersin, Digital HR Leaders, DealMakers).

name: Matthew Thompson
current_role: President & Chief Commercial Officer, Socure (identity verification), since Dec 2025
profile: Former Army Ranger and Harvard MBA who co-founded ID.me (begun 2010 as TroopSwap, a military deals site) with HBS classmate Blake Hall and served as its COO/president; left in 2015. Later ran IDEMIA's North America identity business and held an identity role at Capital One, then joined Socure, building its public-sector business before becoming CRO and, in Dec 2025, President & CCO.
interesting_fact: ID.me began as an HBS project: Hall and Thompson, both Army veterans, struggled to claim veteran discounts online. Thompson had gone to Goldman Sachs in Los Angeles after his MBA but came back when Hall opened shop near D.C. in early 2011.
deep_cut_fact: He holds three patents spanning mobile biometric liveness detection and tiered and third-party authentication, and was Socure's first public-sector leader, launching its government business.
notes: No longer at ID.me (left 2015 per Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ID.me); best route is via Socure's PR agency (Highwire). Common name - confirm via ID.me/Socure context.

name: Roman Itskovich
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Risk Officer, At-Bay (cyber insurance, Mountain View/Tel Aviv)
profile: Israeli-born co-founder of At-Bay (2016, with CEO Rotem Iram), a cyber insurer that pairs policies with active security monitoring ('insure-sec'). At-Bay has raised ~$295M from backers including Khosla, Lightspeed and M12 and reached unicorn status. As Chief Risk Officer he runs underwriting/risk and speaks publicly on cyber-market pricing discipline.
interesting_fact: At-Bay made Forbes' Fintech 50 list in 2023; Itskovich has publicly warned that 'irresponsible' competition in the cyber insurance market is unsustainable as threats rise.
deep_cut_fact: Before insurance he was VP of Financial Products at FX fintech Ebury, on Bain Capital's investment team, and a McKinsey consultant; he holds a BA in Economics and Accounting from Tel Aviv University and an HBS MBA.
notes: Has appeared on insurance podcasts (Behind the Growth, Making Risk Flow) - receptive to talking about cyber risk. Route via press@at-bay.com.

name: Mohit Garg
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, OLOID (passwordless workforce identity, Sunnyvale CA); co-founder of Mindtickle
profile: One of four co-founders (with Krishna Depura, Deepak Diwakar and Nishant Mungali) of Pune-born Mindtickle, which pivoted from gamification to onboarding to sales enablement and became a unicorn in Aug 2021. In 2018 he co-founded OLOID, a passwordless/physical-identity platform for frontline workers, which has raised ~$23M Series A/A1 from Dell Technologies Capital, Honeywell, Okta Ventures and Yaletown.
interesting_fact: Mindtickle was the product of three pivots: it began in 2011 as a gamification platform, moved to employee onboarding, then to sales-rep productivity before reaching a $1B+ valuation.
deep_cut_fact: The Mindtickle idea began with online 'treasure hunts' the founders ran for fun - they later converted those treasure hunts into a way to engage and onboard new employees.
notes: Now focused on OLOID rather than Mindtickle (listed as Mindtickle co-founder/advisor). Appeared on Founder Thesis podcast ('Once Tickled, Twice OLOID'). No dedicated press email found; OLOID site has Contact Us form/newsroom.

name: Sean Henry
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Stord (commerce enablement / fulfillment, Atlanta)
profile: Atlanta native who co-founded Stord with Jacob Boudreau in 2015 as a Georgia Tech freshman, dropping out at 19. Stord provides warehousing, fulfillment and software that give independent brands Amazon-like shipping; a $250M Series F reportedly valued it around $3B. Thiel Fellow, Forbes 30 Under 30 (2019) and named by Forbes in 2021 the youngest CEO of a $1B+ company.
interesting_fact: Forbes recognized him in 2021 as the youngest CEO of a $1B+ company; he founded Stord at 18.
deep_cut_fact: The Stord idea crystallized days before his first Georgia Tech classes, while telling his family about his summer job at a manufacturer in Germany. He also dropped out before learning he'd won the Thiel Fellowship: 'I jumped two feet in and hoped they said yes later.'
notes: Accessible, media-friendly founder (Entrepreneur bylines, Not Another CEO interview). Logistics/supply-chain angle fits the podcast.
